Image Compressor for Online Forms

Many application portals set a maximum size in KB and a required format. Use this page to prepare a photo or signature, then check it against the portal’s own rules.

Compression tool

Target size Target size:
Advanced settings

By default the tool keeps quality reasonable (about 62% or higher) and reduces dimensions to reach small targets; tick “Keep dimensions” to prefer full size at lower quality. Aspect ratio is always preserved and images are never enlarged. PNG is lossless and may not reach a small target; JPEG/WebP are lossy. JPEG replaces transparency with white; WebP and PNG keep it.

Before you start

Read the form’s requirements: maximum KB, accepted formats (often JPG), and any pixel dimensions. ImageTo20KB cannot know a specific portal’s rules, so always confirm them.

Photos and signatures

Set the target to the form’s maximum, choose JPEG, and, if exact pixel dimensions are required, resize with the Image Resizer first.

Check the result

After processing, confirm the final size and dimensions in the result card before uploading.

Why forms reject images

Online forms commonly reject uploads for three reasons: the file is too large, the format is wrong, or the pixel dimensions do not match. This page helps with the first two and partly with the third. It cannot guarantee acceptance, because every portal has its own rules and sometimes changes them.

Always read the instructions on the form itself, including minimum sizes. Some portals require not only a maximum size but also a minimum, for example "between 20KB and 50KB". The result card shows the exact size so you can check both.

Preparing a passport-style photo

Use a clear, well-lit photo with a plain background and crop to the framing the form requests before compressing. Then pick the maximum size in KB and choose JPEG. If the form states pixel dimensions, use the image resizer to match them closely, keeping in mind that this tool preserves aspect ratio and does not crop.

Signatures and scanned documents

Sign on plain white paper with a dark pen, photograph or scan it in even light, crop tightly, and compress. Signatures typically fit very small limits. For scanned certificates, keep the width large enough that small print stays readable, and check the result at full size before uploading.

Government, exam and job portals

These portals frequently set limits such as 20KB, 50KB or 100KB, and some count 1KB as 1,000 bytes. Because this site uses 1,024 bytes per KB, leave a little headroom if the limit is strict. We are not affiliated with any exam body, government site or employer, and we cannot confirm a specific portal's rules.

A short checklist before you upload

Confirm the maximum and minimum size in KB, the allowed formats, the required pixel dimensions, and whether the file name has restrictions. Compress the image, check the result card, rename the file if the portal requires a simple name, and keep the original. If a portal still rejects the image, read the error message carefully, because it often names the exact problem.

Why a smaller file is not always accepted

Some portals check dimensions or the shape of the picture as well as the size. Others reject unusual JPEG variants. This tool creates standard JPEG, WebP or PNG files, but it cannot guarantee that a given portal will accept them.

Privacy when handling ID photos

Photos and signatures are personal. The compression itself happens in your browser and the image is not uploaded for compression. Still, treat downloaded files carefully: delete copies you no longer need, avoid using shared computers for sensitive documents, and close the tab when you are finished so that the browser releases the images from memory.

Keep a record of what you submitted

Save the compressed file you actually uploaded, with a clear name and date. If a portal later asks you to re-upload, you can reuse it, and if something goes wrong you can see exactly what was sent.

Common questions

Will my file be accepted by every portal?

Not guaranteed. Each portal has its own rules; this tool only prepares the file size and format.
